questions.q: What specifically triggers a merge conflict?
options: Merging any two branches that have ever diverged
Both branches changing the exact same lines of the exact same file in different ways
Running git merge without first running git fetch
Having more than two branches in a repository
questions.explain: Git can automatically combine changes that don't overlap. A conflict happens only when both branches modified the same lines differently, and Git has no way to know which version is correct.

questions.q: In a conflict marker block, what does the section between <<<<<<< HEAD and ======= represent?
options: The incoming branch's version of the content
Your currently checked-out branch's version of the content
A deleted version that will be discarded automatically
The original common ancestor's version
questions.explain: The content between <<<<<<< HEAD and ======= is your current branch's version; the content between ======= and the >>>>>>> marker is the incoming branch's version.

questions.q: After manually resolving a conflicted file by removing the conflict markers, what's the next step?
options: Delete the file and recreate it
Run git merge --abort
git add the resolved file, then git commit to complete the merge
Nothing further is needed — Git detects the resolution automatically
questions.explain: Once a file's conflicts are resolved, you stage it with git add just like any other change, then git commit to finish the merge (Git pre-fills a merge commit message).

options: Permanently deletes the branch being merged
Commits the conflict markers as-is
Cancels the in-progress conflicted merge and restores the state from before the merge started
Force-pushes the current branch to overwrite the remote
questions.explain: git merge --abort safely cancels a paused, conflicted merge and returns the repository to exactly how it was before the merge began — nothing is lost since nothing was committed.

questions.q: If a merge produces conflicts in three different files, how does git status describe them during the paused merge?
options: It only reports the first conflicted file and hides the rest
It lists every conflicted file under "Unmerged paths," all needing resolution before committing
It automatically resolves two of the three and asks about only one
It refuses to run until all conflicts are resolved
questions.explain: git status during a conflicted merge lists every file still containing unresolved conflicts under "Unmerged paths" — each one needs to be resolved and staged before the merge commit can be made.
